html_en:
The next phase of AI development is becoming clear: it's not about better chatbots, but about agents that actually get work done — and that reality is shifting faster than most realize.

Building for the Exponential

At Code with Claude this week, Anthropic's leaders painted a picture of AI development that's far beyond incremental improvements. Peter Yang captured some striking insights from Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei's session:
"Build for the exponential. There are products that are not possible with the current model but could work with later models. This puts a premium on internal experimentation. You have to just try it with the model to see if it works."
This philosophy is already paying dividends. Dario revealed that Anthropic "saw 80x growth earlier this year on usage and revenue" — a staggering figure that explains their aggressive compute acquisition strategy. As @trq212 highlighted, Dario's message was clear:
"everyday we're trying to obtain more compute to pass on to you, we're sorry if it takes sometime but we're going to acquire as much as we can."
The implications are profound. As the Anthropic team noted,
"Products reach their saturation when models get too good. The ways in which we are making models smarter today are much more evident in agentic and Claude Code workflows than chatbots."

The Coding Revolution Is Already Here

Perhaps nowhere is this exponential shift more visible than in software development itself. Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, shared remarkable insights in a Training Data podcast session that reveals just how far we've come. Zara Zhang captured the most memorable moments: Boris casually mentioning he has "thousands" of agents running overnight, his near-exclusive use of Claude Code on mobile, and his prediction that
"Coding will become the new literacy, just like reading and writing."
The numbers are staggering. In the podcast, Boris revealed that he now writes
"a few dozen PRs every day"
with a record of
"150 PRs in a day"
— all generated by AI. For him,
"the model writes 100% of my code"
as of October-November 2024. This isn't just about productivity gains; it's about a fundamental shift in how software gets built. Boris explained how Claude Code initially struggled for six months until it hit an inflection point:
"That started with Opus four in May... it just kind of keeps inflecting."

Agents That Actually Learn and Improve

Anthropic isn't just making models that code better — they're building systems that get smarter over time. The company announced two significant agent capabilities that signal where this is all heading. Dreaming represents a breakthrough in agent memory:
"Dreaming reviews your agent's past sessions, extracts patterns, and curates memories so your agents learn over time."
Meanwhile, Outcomes addresses the quality control challenge:
"Outcomes lets you set the bar for quality. You write a rubric, a separate grader checks the output, and the agent iterates until it gets there."
These aren't just features — they're the building blocks of truly autonomous systems that can maintain standards and accumulate knowledge.

The New Technical Debt Paradox

As AI accelerates development cycles, Anthropic's leadership identified an intriguing paradox. As Yang noted, Dario observed:
"It's easy to accumulate an extraordinary amount of internal tech debt when you ship that fast. But the models can also help you pay down this debt."
This suggests we're entering a new equilibrium where AI both creates and solves technical complexity at unprecedented speeds. The models are
"evolving from coding to software engineering to just growing a business"
— a progression that hints at AI's expansion beyond pure technical tasks into strategic business functions. The transformation is happening faster than most anticipated, and those building for today's capabilities may find themselves quickly outdated. As the Anthropic team emphasized, the premium now is on "internal experimentation" — constantly testing what becomes possible with each model improvement rather than optimizing for current limitations.
html_zh:
今天的人工智能圈围绕一个主题展开：基础设施正在重塑一切，从编程到企业运营，再到我们对技术演进的理解。

Anthropic 的指数级增长与计算资源争夺战

在最新的公开场合，Anthropic 的首席执行官 Dario Amodei 透露了令人震惊的增长数据。Peter Yang 转述了这位 CEO 的话：

"我们今年早些时候看到了使用量和收入的 80 倍增长"

这一数字背后的紧迫性体现在 Dario 的后续表态中——"每天我们都在努力获取更多算力传递给你们，如果需要一些时间我们很抱歉，但我们会尽可能多地获取算力"。

这种对算力的渴求不仅仅是商业需要，更反映了 AI 模型能力提升的根本逻辑。正如 Dario 在同场活动中所说：

"为指数级发展而构建。有些产品在当前模型上不可能实现，但在未来的模型上可以运行。这对内部实验提出了更高要求。你必须用模型亲自尝试，看看是否有效。"

编程的印刷机时刻

如果说计算资源是 AI 发展的燃料，那么编程工具的革命就是这场变革最直观的体现。Zara Zhang 分享了与 Boris Cherny（Claude Code 的创造者）的采访中最令人印象深刻的几点：

- Boris 随口提到他在夜间运行着"数千个"代理
- Boris 说他现在几乎只在手机上使用 Claude Code
- 编程将成为新的读写能力，就像阅读和写作一样

在 Training Data 播客的采访中，Boris 详细阐述了这一转变。他描述了自己如何从一个每天手写代码的工程师，转变为 100% 依赖 AI 代理编程的开发者：

"对我来说，模型编写了 100% 的代码。我通常每天写几十个 PR。上周有一天我做了 150 个 PR，那是个记录。我只是想看看能推进到什么程度。"

这种转变的时间线也很关键。Boris 透露，Claude Code 最初"六个月都不太好用"，真正的指数级增长始于今年 5 月 Opus 4 的发布。

智能体时代的产品哲学

Anthropic 今天发布了两个重要的智能体功能：Dreaming 和 Outcomes。前者让智能体能够"审查过去的会话，提取模式，并整理记忆，使你的智能体随时间学习"；后者则"让你设定质量标准。你写一个评分标准，单独的评分器检查输出，智能体迭代直到达到标准"。

这些功能背后反映的是 Dario 在采访中提到的更深层洞察：

"当模型变得太好时，产品会达到饱和点。我们今天让模型更智能的方式，在智能体和 Claude Code 工作流中比在聊天机器人中更加明显。你必须思考下一个大事件是什么。"
"模型正在从编程发展到软件工程，再到经营企业。"

技术债务的新解决方案

在快速发展的同时，技术债务问题依然存在。但 Dario 提出了一个有趣的观点：

"当你快速发布时，很容易积累大量的内部技术债务。但模型也可以帮助你偿还这些债务。"

这种观点代表了对传统软件开发思维的根本性重新思考。如果 AI 模型既能快速创建代码，也能帮助重构和优化现有代码，那么"快速行动，破除陈规"的哲学可能真正成为可持续的开发策略。

正如 Garry Tan 风趣地比喻，在这场 AI 革命中，每个参与者都像是《低俗小说》中的"清洁工"——我们正在清理旧的工作方式，为全新的生产力范式让路。而从今天的种种迹象来看，这个转变比我们想象的来得更快、更彻底。
